question: Who are traditionally believed to have composed the Vedic hymns in early Indian tradition?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Rishis and Rishikas**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In early Indian tradition, the **Vedic hymns** were composed by **Rishis** (sages) and **Rishikas** (female sages). These hymns form part of the sacred texts of the Vedas, which are the earliest literary and religious texts of ancient India.
 
• The Rishis and Rishikas were believed to have been divinely inspired and had the spiritual insight to hear and compose these sacred hymns, known as "Shruti," meaning "that which is heard."
 
• The hymns mainly comprise prayers, praises, and philosophical discourses dedicated to various deities such as Agni (fire), Indra (rain and thunder), and Varuna (cosmic order).
 
• These compositions were passed down orally through generations before being written down, showcasing the oral tradition of ancient India.
 
• The Vedic hymns encapsulate knowledge related to cosmology, rituals, ethics, and philosophical inquiry, forming the foundation of Hinduism and Indian culture.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Rishis and Rishikas:**

 
 
• The term "Rishi" refers to a sage or seer in ancient Indian tradition who was spiritually enlightened and capable of divine insight.
 
• Female sages, known as "Rishikas," also contributed to the composition of some hymns in the Vedas. For instance, notable Rishikas include **Gargi** and **Maitreyi**, who appear in philosophical discussions in texts like the Upanishads.
 
• Rishis were often regarded as the mediators between humans and the divine realm, interpreting cosmic truths through their hymns.
 
 
 
• **Vedas:**
 
 
• The Vedas consist of four collections: **Rigveda, Samaveda, Yajurveda,** and **Atharvaveda**. Each collection has its unique focus, ranging from hymns to rituals and philosophical discourses.
 
• The Rigveda, the oldest of the Vedas, contains more than 1,000 hymns dedicated to various deities.
 
• The Vedas were composed in **Vedic Sanskrit**, a language distinct from Classical Sanskrit and believed to be one of the oldest languages in the world.
 
 
 
• **Oral Tradition:**
 
 
• The Vedic hymns were transmitted orally for centuries before being written down, demonstrating a remarkable tradition of memorization and preservation.
 
• The oral tradition involved intricate techniques of recitation to ensure accuracy, including methods such as **Padapatha** and **Krama Patha**.
 
 
 
• **Philosophical Contribution:**
 
 
• The hymns composed by Rishis and Rishikas laid the groundwork for later philosophical texts like the Upanishads, which delve deeper into metaphysical concepts such as **Brahman** (ultimate reality) and **Atman** (soul).
 
• These texts also discuss the nature of existence, the universe, and the relationship between the divine and the individual.
 
 
 
• **Other Options Explained:**
 
 
• **Kings:** Kings in early Indian tradition were often patrons of religion and culture but did not compose the Vedic hymns.
 
• **Scholars from Nalanda:** Nalanda University was established much later, during the Gupta period, and its scholars mainly focused on Buddhist teachings and other disciplines.
 
• **Village Elders:** Village elders played important roles in local governance and social rituals but were not the composers of the Vedic hymns.
